kit marlowe was the literary john the baptist to shakespeare. kit nearly failed college because he missed many exams while working for queen elizabeth, but she passed him with a single letter of excuse. i think mr. marlowe was an atheist around the time he wrote "the jew of malta," and he saw or learned of necromancy in the queen's court--- likely performed by edward kelly with help of her personal astrologer john dee (about which ben jonson wrote "the alchemist") as testified to by meric casaubon (whose huguenot father first translated aurelius)--- but, by an encounter with satan's "spiritual wickedness in high places," marlowe had a change of heart which manifested in a bold public expose , a play he wrote called faust, for which royalty had him assassinated under the old reproachful guise that marlowe was an argumentative atheist drunkard who could give more reasons for unbelief than any theologian could for belief, and-- in accordance with his base nature-- got himself stabbed through the eye in a pub for such proud contention. strange! at once, both intimate tool of highest royalty and elizabethan literary power only eclipsed by shakespeare himself, but yet lowest pub-dwelling scoundrel killed in bickering!? to think, sir francis bacon (the bribe/gift taker) had raleigh executed (didn't he?), bacon, friend of dr. dee the wizard.... and raleigh supposedly attended marlowe's dark lectures, but raleigh's later "history of the world" asserts god's existence, and so does his last letter to his wife before he died. did he too repent of atheism? did satan drive him to god? surely, manifestations of occult power can backfire like that. idk. what remains are stories about his vile son being reluctantly invited to a feast among great men, saying: "i, this morning, not having the fear of god before my eyes but by the instigation of the devil, went to a whore. i was very eager of her, kissed her, and went to enjoy her, but she thrust me from her, and vowed i should not,  for your father lay with me but an hour ago.  sir walt, being so strangely surprised and put out of his countenance at so great a table, gives his son a damned blow over the face. his son, as rude as he was, would not strike his father, but strikes over the face of a gentleman that sat next to him, and said,  box about,  twill come to my father anon'" (aubrey's "short biographies").this new puritan dares to confess that the demons, which manifested to his heart that was once bent toward demonalotry, helped flip the illuminating switch on the reality of god in his life, no matter what the case was with marlowe and raleigh. for this he renders thanks to the everlasting father and prince of peace: christ the lord. 1. did the illuminati activate in 1776? 4. i thought it may be helpful to share ways we all save money. i don't know about you all, but as a family of 7 and with prices going up, we need to find ways to pinch pennies. everyone's lists will be different and that's perfectly fine. it is what makes us unique. so please no judgment.   1. we don't have a heat/air system. surely that has saved us something. though these days it is much harder to tell.2. we gather free firewood, by hand from people who need brush and trees taken out 3. we cook from scratch and rarely eat out. using basic ingredients, we cut out all of those prepackaged dead foods. which also keeps us healthy and far from a doctor. that's a bonus!4. we only use a dryer in bad weather. and once our dryer goes to dryer heaven, we have no intentions on replacing it. a clothesline is a good thing!5. we replaced our toilets with compost toilets built from pallets. the secret here is mulch. 6. we haven't bought toilet paper since before covid was a thing. we use cloth and rags. seeing as how we had a little one in cloth diapers, and they needed washed and hung on the line, it only made sense... same goes with feminine products!7. we attempt to grow and raise all of our food. some years are better than others, but every little bit counts. we also don't pay to have someone else do the animal processing. that happens here as a family.8. we have very few appliances other than refrigerator, freezer and washer. most of the lightbulbs in our home have been removed. we don't use a dishwasher, microwave, toaster, etc. we also don't have a television. we read instead.9. we make our own home care products. there is an upfront cost, but in the long run you save. we also make the majority of our herbal infusions, tinctures, syrups and salves.10. we keep a compost bin. also use deep bedding method for our poultry and keep a worm bin. any other extra kitchen scraps go to the pigs. 11. speaking of deep bedding, we had 10 tons of free wood chips brought in. the chickens work for us and scratch it up, turning it into a lovely compost for the garden. also used in the composting toilet.13. we shop second hand. buy used and save the difference! 14. we buy in bulk when possible. you can get basics at a much lower cost 15. we make our own entertainment. i cannot tell you the last time we went to a movie or concert. 15 years possibly? our friends think us odd that someone in their mid 30s wouldn't want to do what the world does. getting my hair done, or my nails. nah, i would much rather improve something on the homestead or learn a new skill.i could go on and on. these are just a few ways we save. i could also probably make just as large of a list of things that need improvement. but this is a journey. we may never fully get there. i would love to hear ways you save money during these hard times.
